item.commandcookies_electronic_mod.airpo: Right-click to wear, or use the head slot.
item.commandcookies_electronic_mod.aa_ba: Powers the camera for 15 real days.
Right-click a security camera with 2 AA batteries.
commandcookies_electronic_mod.guide.head: SETUP GUIDE
commandcookies_electronic_mod.guide.powe: Put the Generator on the floor. It burns furnace fuel to make electricity.
Right-click it to open its menu, then put Coal or any furnace fuel in the FUEL slot. It shows ONLINE while fuel burns; press Start if it shows PAUSED.
Place a Wall Power Outlet on a solid wall. A generator can supply outlets up to 120 blocks away.
Right-click the Generator with a Wrench, then right-click the outlet. Outlets in range light up after the first click. The feed cable powers the outlet.
Mount the TV within 15 blocks of the outlet. Wrench the outlet, then the TV, to plug in its power cord. The screen turns on.
Power flows generator → outlet → TV. Right-click the TV to choose an Imgur image; this picture is a sample. Each outlet has two sockets. Sneak-right-click with the Wrench to unplug.
commandcookies_electronic_mod.guide.stan: Place the TV with Stand on a solid surface two blocks wide; it faces you.
Wrench a powered outlet within 15 blocks, then the TV. The screen turns on, black until you choose an image.
Right-click the TV, paste an Imgur link, pick Whole image or Fill screen, then press Apply & Close. This picture is a sample.
Sneak-right-click the TV with the Wrench to unplug it. Only the wall-mounted TV has swivel, tilt and rotation sliders.
commandcookies_electronic_mod.guide.crt_: Place the CRT TV; it faces you. It needs two cords: wall power and coax.
Wrench a powered Wall Power Outlet, then the CRT TV. It stays dark: the picture needs coax as well.
Wrench a powered Wall Coax Outlet, then the TV. With both cords live, the screen lights up.
Sneak-right-click the CRT TV with the Wrench to unplug both cords at once. It has no image menu and no AV input.
commandcookies_electronic_mod.guide.retr: The Retro Monitor is the display for the NES, SNES and N64 consoles. Place it facing you.
Wrench a Wall Power Outlet, then the monitor; then a Wall Coax Outlet, then the monitor. It turns on once both are live.
Wrench power to a console, then right-click the console and the monitor with an AV Cable. One console per monitor, up to 16 blocks.
Hold the console's own controller and right-click the monitor. NES Tetris works in the base mod; your own ROM games need the optional Retro Expansion.
commandcookies_electronic_mod.guide.gene: Put the Generator on solid ground; it faces you. It burns furnace fuel to power wall outlets.

Right-click it to open its menu and put Coal or any furnace fuel in the FUEL slot; hoppers can fill it too. One coal lasts about 2 h 37 min of play. The menu shows ONLINE, NO FUEL or PAUSED and the fuel time left.
Press Pause in the menu to switch it off without using fuel, and Start to run it again. Its outlets lose power while it is paused or out of fuel.
Right-click the Generator with a Wrench, then a Wall Power or Wall Coax Outlet. Outlets within 120 blocks light up; one generator can feed many outlets.
Devices plug into an outlet, never the generator: wrench the outlet, then a device within 15 blocks. The generator only runs while its chunk is loaded.
commandcookies_electronic_mod.guide.wren: Right-click a generator, outlet or device with the Wrench; blocks it can link to light up. Click the same block again to clear the selection. It also expires after two minutes.
Then right-click a highlighted outlet. The feed cable reaches up to 120 blocks, and the selection clears after each link.
Wrench an outlet and a device within 15 blocks, in either order, to plug in its cord. Power outlets have two sockets; coax outlets have one and fit only the CRT TV and retro monitor.
Sneak-right-click a device with the Wrench to unplug its power and coax cords, or an outlet to cut its generator feed. Sneak-clicking the generator clears your selection.
Generators to outlets; outlets to TVs, the CRT TV, retro monitor, NES, SNES, N64, gaming PC and gaming monitor. Cameras run on batteries, and HDMI and AV links use their own cables.
commandcookies_electronic_mod.guide.powe: Right-click the side of a solid block to mount a Wall Power Outlet. Right-click it with an empty hand to see whether it has power.
Wrench the Generator, then the outlet, up to 120 blocks away. The outlet lights up while its generator runs.
Wrench the outlet, then a device within 15 blocks. Its power cord takes the upper socket, and this TV switches on.
A second device takes the lower socket, so one outlet powers two devices at once.
A third device is refused: the outlet already has two cables. Use another outlet, or sneak-wrench a plugged-in device to free its socket.
TVs, the CRT TV, retro monitor, NES, SNES, N64, gaming PC and gaming monitor. The CRT TV and retro monitor also need a coax outlet; cameras and laptops need no outlet.
commandcookies_electronic_mod.guide.coax: Right-click the side of a solid block to mount a Wall Coax Outlet. It carries the picture signal and has a single socket.
Coax outlets need power too: wrench the Generator, then the coax outlet, up to 120 blocks away.
Wrench the coax outlet, then a CRT TV or retro monitor within 15 blocks. With coax alone the display stays dark.
Wrench a Wall Power Outlet, then the same display. With power and coax both live, it turns on.
A coax outlet holds one cable and refuses a second display. Give each CRT TV or retro monitor its own coax outlet.
commandcookies_electronic_mod.guide.came: Right-click the side of a solid block to mount a Security Camera; it looks out from the wall. Whoever places it owns it.
Right-click the camera holding AA Batteries. It takes two, from anywhere in your inventory, and runs for 15 real-world days.
Cameras never use a wrench, outlet or generator. Right-click with an empty hand to see the battery time left; new batteries go in once they run out.
The owner right-clicks the camera holding an iPhone or Samsung phone to pair it. Up to 16 phones per camera; pairings last until the camera is broken.
Right-click the phone in the air and open its Security app to view paired cameras from anywhere. Open laptops and BlockOS PCs list your own cameras within 64 blocks.
commandcookies_electronic_mod.guide.pc.s: Place a Gaming PC and a Gaming Monitor facing you. Black and white models work the same and can be mixed.
Right-click the monitor holding a Keyboard, then a Mouse, to attach them to its desk. They are optional; crouch-right-click with an empty hand removes them, mouse first.
The PC and the monitor each need their own Wrench link to a powered outlet within 15 blocks. One outlet's two sockets can serve both.
Right-click the PC, then the monitor, with an HDMI Cable, up to 16 blocks apart. Both switch on once linked and powered.
Right-click the monitor to open BlockOS on its PC. Clicking the PC itself only reports whether it is ready.
Crouch-right-click either device with an HDMI Cable to unlink them; the cable drops back. Sneak-wrench a device to unplug its power.
commandcookies_electronic_mod.guide.hdmi: An HDMI Cable links exactly one Gaming PC to one Gaming Monitor, black or white, up to 16 blocks apart.
Right-click the PC (or the monitor) with the HDMI Cable. Unlinked devices of the other kind light up.
Right-click the monitor to connect. One cable is used (none in Creative), and both devices come on if each has wall power.
Crouch-right-click either device with an HDMI Cable to unlink; the cable drops back. A linked device must be unlinked before it can join another.
HDMI carries only the picture: each device keeps its own Wrench link to an outlet. Laptops need no HDMI or power at all.
commandcookies_electronic_mod.guide.av.s: An AV Cable connects one NES, SNES or N64 to one Retro Monitor, up to 16 blocks apart. It does not fit the CRT TV.
Right-click the console (or the monitor) with the AV Cable. Unlinked devices it can reach light up.
Right-click the monitor to plug in the cable. One AV Cable is used (none in Creative).
Crouch-right-click either end with an AV Cable to unplug it; the cable drops back. Each monitor takes one console at a time.
AV carries only the game picture. The console needs wall power, and the monitor needs wall power and coax.
Place a NES console beside a Retro Monitor, both facing you.
Wrench a powered outlet to the NES, then to the monitor. The monitor also needs coax: wrench a Wall Coax Outlet, then the monitor.
Right-click the NES, then the monitor, with an AV Cable, up to 16 blocks apart.
Right-click a NES ROM Cartridge in the air, import or pick one of your own .nes games, then right-click the NES with it. The base mod's NES Tetris Cartridge also works.
Hold the NES Controller in either hand and right-click the monitor. The game screen shows its keyboard controls.
Crouch-right-click the NES to eject the cartridge. Crouch-right-click either device with the AV Cable to unplug it.
commandcookies_electronic_mod.guide.snes: Place a SNES console beside a Retro Monitor, both facing you.
Wrench a powered outlet to the SNES and to the monitor, then a Wall Coax Outlet to the monitor.
Right-click the SNES, then the monitor, with an AV Cable, up to 16 blocks apart. Without the Retro Expansion the SNES stays decorative after this step.
Retro Expansion required: right-click a SNES ROM Cartridge in the air, import or pick one of your own .sfc or .smc games (none are included), then right-click the SNES with it.
Hold the SNES Controller in either hand and right-click the monitor to play in the Retro Expansion. Its keyboard controls appear on the game screen.
Crouch-right-click the SNES to eject the cartridge. Crouch-right-click either device with the AV Cable to unplug it.
Place an N64 console beside a Retro Monitor, both facing you.
Wrench a powered outlet to the N64 and to the monitor, then a Wall Coax Outlet to the monitor.
Right-click the N64, then the monitor, with an AV Cable, up to 16 blocks apart. Without the Retro Expansion the N64 stays decorative after this step.
Retro Expansion required: right-click an N64 ROM Cartridge in the air, import or pick one of your own .z64, .n64 or .v64 games (none are included), then right-click the N64 with it.
Hold the N64 Controller in either hand and right-click the monitor to play in the Retro Expansion. The game screen shows the keys, including the analog stick.
Crouch-right-click the N64 to eject the cartridge. Crouch-right-click either device with the AV Cable to unplug it.
commandcookies_electronic_mod.guide.nes_: Place a NES console beside a Retro Monitor, both facing you.
Wrench a powered outlet to the NES, then to the monitor. The monitor also needs coax: wrench a Wall Coax Outlet, then the monitor.
Right-click the NES, then the monitor, with an AV Cable, up to 16 blocks apart.
Right-click the NES holding the NES Tetris Cartridge to insert it.
Hold the NES Controller in either hand and right-click the monitor. Tetris needs no addon; the game screen lists its keyboard controls.
Crouch-right-click the NES to eject the cartridge. Crouch-right-click either device with the AV Cable to unplug it.
commandcookies_electronic_mod.guide.snes: Place a SNES console beside a Retro Monitor, both facing you.
Wrench a powered outlet to the SNES and to the monitor, then a Wall Coax Outlet to the monitor.
Right-click the SNES, then the monitor, with an AV Cable, up to 16 blocks apart.
The SNES is decorative in the base mod. Retro Expansion adds gameplay. Crouch-right-click either end with the AV Cable to unplug it.
commandcookies_electronic_mod.guide.n64_: Place an N64 console beside a Retro Monitor, both facing you.
Wrench a powered outlet to the N64 and to the monitor, then a Wall Coax Outlet to the monitor.
Right-click the N64, then the monitor, with an AV Cable, up to 16 blocks apart.
The N64 is decorative in the base mod. Retro Expansion adds gameplay. Crouch-right-click either end with the AV Cable to unplug it.
commandcookies_electronic_mod.guide.retr: The Retro Monitor is the display for the NES, SNES and N64 consoles. Place it facing you.
Wrench a Wall Power Outlet, then the monitor; then a Wall Coax Outlet, then the monitor. It turns on once both are live.
Wrench power to a console, then right-click the console and the monitor with an AV Cable. One console per monitor, up to 16 blocks.
Insert a NES Tetris Cartridge into the linked NES, hold its controller and right-click the monitor. SNES and N64 setups are decorative in the base mod.
